findings.finding: A blocked doctor now prints the driver's 'ok' and then exits 1. warden's upstream-CA check blocks, doctorBinary still runs the container driver's doctor, whose doctor() prints 'container runtime: <rt>' and 'ok' (command.go:136) straight to stdout, and only then does warden os.Exit(1). The same happens for a driver binary that lists no doctor (host.go:419-423 prints 'ok' before exiting 1 when blocked). main printed no 'ok' when blocked. The approved design lists this under what does not change ('Exit codes (UX-09): ... and 1 for a blocked doctor with no extra line', Behaviour, design line 4392), and it is not among the nineteen accepted changes. Implement kept it and changed TestUpstreamCALinesOfDoctor's two blocked cases to expect 'ok', so the test now holds the deviation. An 'ok' line followed by exit 1 is also a contradictory report for a user and a script.
findings.fix: No design change is needed: DRV-25 only says doctor reports on stdout and returns blocked, and does not say who prints 'ok'. Make 'ok' warden's: drop the Fprintln(out, "ok") from the container driver's doctor (driver/container/command.go:136), have doctorBinary print 'ok' only when neither warden's part nor the driver's result is blocked (and not at host.go:419 when blocked), and restore TestUpstreamCALinesOfDoctor's blocked cases to main's expectation. The unblocked output stays 'container runtime: <rt>' then 'ok', which is what the macos-finch validation note expects. If Implement prefers to keep the line, it goes back to Design (FLOW-06) to add it to Behaviour.

findings.finding: TestBuildSequenceSignalBeforeTheRelay orders its two events with time.Sleep(10ms). It sends os.Interrupt into a buffered signals channel (cap 1, line 179), sleeps 10 ms, then opens the gate, which makes the driver send relay-started. If the sequence's loop has not yet received the signal when the gate opens (a loaded or -race CI runner), its select sees both the signal and relay-started ready and picks either. When it picks relay-started first, the claim goes ahead and the trace and the 'no claim' assertion fail. A timing-dependent test is a defect under TEST-04.
findings.fix: Wait for the signal to be handled instead of sleeping. For example, have the test's stopSignals close a channel (or set a flag the test polls, like waitFor) and wait on it before close(gate). Or make the test's signals channel unbuffered for this case, so the send returns only once the loop has taken the signal; onSignal then runs before the loop's next select.

findings.finding: The change alters two security boundaries, as the design declares (security_boundary: host-env, and env-relay). (1) host-env: the code that builds the isolation is now chosen at run time by a lookup (PATH first, then beside warden, then linked), with no ownership or mode check (a16 as Jeff answered it). The one guard is that a config file may name a driver, not a file (driverlookup.go findByPath, sourceConfig). (2) env-relay: warden now makes the claim token and claims every driver's relay. The design's Security note covers both. In the code read, the guard is implemented as the note says: a relative or empty PATH entry is an error, on Windows only .exe is a candidate, and a non-executable file is skipped and listed. MUST-review: this needs the human's sign-off at merge, not a fix.
findings.fix: None required. The human acknowledges it at merge (FLOW-08) against the design's Security note. Whether this change trips TEST-08's security suite is that rule's call at release.

warden closes the driver's input straight after writing stop (drivercall.go dialogue), so the kit's reader sees stop and then end of input. pipeHost.Wait can then return 'interrupted' in place of the stop's reason when both are ready. The container driver ignores Wait's value, and its teardown takes no context, so nothing changes today. A driver that branches on the reason could see the wrong one.
